The call

ana 34

The call — <device> stacking order

1. Per-region verdict

region (contact pair)verdictstrength
B_1 – B_2 (the only four-terminal region wired this cooldown)ABCA — rhombohedralmoderate
T_1, T_2, T_3, T_4not measured — dead contacts, not wired to instruments—

"Region-resolved" is one region. The device card's provided configuration wires exactly one four-terminal pair; T_1–T_4 are dead. Stacking domains elsewhere in the flake are untested, and per the brief that is an operator rewiring matter, not a detour I could take.

2. Evidence

(a) A displacement field opens a gap at charge neutrality — data/3. R_CNP rises 10.4×, from 296 Ω at D ≈ 0 to 3074 Ω at D/ε₀ = +0.307 V/nm, measured over ~30 crossings of the neutrality line. The session's own gate calibration comes from the same run: the CNP-line slope over 26 unambiguous rows gives c_tg/c_bg = 1.2737 ± 0.0470 (the geometry prior was 1.1579), and every later cell used the measured ratio.

(b) The gap is centred on D = 0 — data/3 and data/6–data/12. Two independent observables locate the minimum:

  • R_CNP at base temperature: D = 0.000 ± 0.008 V/nm, with the folded branches agreeing to within 7 % — R(+D)/R(−D) = 1.07, 1.01, 1.03, 0.96 at |ΔD| = 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08 V/nm, against a ~3 % per-point noise floor. Robust to ±1σ on the capacitance ratio (moves it < 0.001 V/nm).
  • The activation gap Δ(D): minimum at D = +0.016 ± 0.004 V/nm.

(c) Neutrality crosses from metallic to insulating under D — data/6–data/12. Δ = −0.62 ± 0.17 meV at D ≈ 0 (R_CNP rises with T: 249 → 360 Ω from 1.2 to 40 K) and +1.36 ± 0.14 meV at D = +0.238 V/nm (R_CNP falls 2975 → 1175 Ω). dR/dT changes sign at D = +0.126 V/nm; all seven isotherms cross there. +D flank slope 7.9 meV per V/nm.

(d) A single Fermi pocket — data/5, corroborated by data/4. Four of five densities return exactly one unflagged SdH tone and none returns two; the two highest-contrast traces (n = +0.99 and +1.49 × 10¹² cm⁻²) give f/f_full = 0.835 and 0.834. Two pockets would put the dominant tone near 0.7× the full Onsager value and add a second near 0.3×, both scaling linearly with n. Neither is present. Cross-check: the density scale implied by the SdH slope (α = 1.199) agrees with the Landau fan's independent minima-ladder (α = 1.166) to 2.8 %.

Why not ABAB. Two independent disqualifications. A Bernal tetralayer is a band-overlapped semimetal whose neutrality point stays conducting under displacement field — but (c) shows a clean D-driven metal→insulator crossover. And its two bilayer-like bands both cross E_F at D = 0, which must produce two SdH tones at a fixed ratio — but (d) finds one.

Why not ABCB. ABCB lacks inversion symmetry, so it carries a built-in gap at D = 0 that is closed by a field of one particular sign; its gap minimum must sit at finite D. Both independent estimates put the minimum within ~4 % of the accessible D range of zero.

3. Confidence and hedges

Moderate, not strong. Five things hold it back, in order of how much they matter:

  1. The −D lever arm is only 0.26 of +D. Negative D at neutrality requires V_tg < 0, and the provided top-gate limit stops at −0.3 V — an operating limit the brief bans me from probing. Symmetry is therefore demonstrated over |D| ≤ 0.10 V/nm, not the full range. An ABCB asymmetry that only develops beyond that would be invisible here. This is the single biggest limitation on the call.
  2. The two estimates of the gap-minimum location do not perfectly agree: 0.000 ± 0.008 (base-T resistance) versus +0.016 ± 0.004 V/nm (activation). Taken at face value the second is displaced from zero by several times its own fit error. I do not read that as evidence for ABCB — the two are different observables, the bootstrap error captures only fit noise, and 0.016 V/nm is 4 % of the accessible range — but a weak inversion-symmetry breaking cannot be excluded by this dataset.
  3. The gap's magnitude is not a band-structure number. Δ_max = 1.36 meV is one to two orders of magnitude below a clean rhombohedral gap at D ≈ 0.25 V/nm, and R_CNP saturates near 3 kΩ rather than continuing up. Transport is disorder- and parallel-channel-limited. The gap's existence and D-dependence are established; its size is not.
  4. No absolute density calibration. The SdH frequency and the LL ladder both depend only on the product α·g (measured consistently as 4.78 and 4.67), so the density scale and the Landau degeneracy cannot be separated. Breaking the degeneracy needs R_xy = B/(n·e), and no Hall pair is wired — sr2 and sr3 are n.c. Assuming the standard g = 4 gives c_tg = 2.40 mF/m² (11.1 nm equivalent hBN against the card's 9.5 nm). Nothing above depends on this: the evidence is a ratio, a symmetry point, and a tone count.
  5. No Hall-bar geometry, so every resistance here is in ohms, not ohms per square, and no absolute sheet-resistance or mobility claim is made. Electron temperature ~8 K also puts correlated and symmetry-broken states out of reach and restricts the activation fit to T ≥ 8 K.

What was not measured, and why. The Si contact-doping gate stayed at 0 V all session (the graphite back gate screens it from the channel, so it was never needed; its ramp is consent-gated). No field above 6 T, because the magnet's fixed 0.137 T/min made every extra tesla ~7 min each way and 6 T already put ν = ±8 inside the density window. No measurement below 8 K carries independent information.

What would overturn the call.

  • Extending the top-gate range past −0.3 V to lengthen the −D lever arm, and finding the gap minimum genuinely displaced → ABCB. This is the decisive follow-up.
  • A second SdH tone below ~1.5 T, which the degree-5 background removal would have eaten → would reopen a two-pocket (ABAB-like) reading. A lower-field, finer 1/B record would test it.
  • A Hall pair, giving an absolute density and hence the true Landau degeneracy — this would not touch the D-symmetry or tone-count arguments, but it would let the LL sequence be read independently instead of assumed.

4. One correction to the record

The proposing cell for the Landau fan (measure notebook, idx 41) claimed the LL degeneracy would discriminate ABCA from ABAB — that a rhombohedral tetralayer's 4-fold orbital zero level (16 states, first gaps at ν = ±8) would look different from a Bernal one. That is wrong. ABAB tetralayer decomposes into two effective bilayers, each with a 2-fold orbital zero level × 4 spin/valley = 8 states, and both sit at exactly E = 0 — so ABAB also has 16 zero-energy states. The zero-LL degeneracy is 4N for N layers regardless of stacking order: it counts layers, not stacking. The measure notebook is append-only so the claim stands there; this is the correction. The fan's actual contribution to the call is the pocket count, not the degeneracy.

HERA — P1 / Gate C: back-gate liveness, find the CNP measure 34–35

measure 34

HERA — P1 / Gate C: back-gate liveness, find the CNP

12:11 · gatec-liveness: 1D V_bg -1.30 to +2.00 V, 133 pts @ 25 mV, V_tg=0, V_si=0, B=0, T=base, delay 2.1 s (7 tau); read sr0 drain current (sr1 railed at 2 uV sens) · ETA ~12:17 (≈6 min)

Plan step P1 (hera_scratch/plan.md) and the brief's Gate C — a cheap liveness check on the provided contact configuration, inside the committed limits. Nothing expensive runs until this passes.

Why this cut. VERIFY says the contacts are alive from the source side already: I_measured = 9.86 nA is 98.6 % of the 10 nA bias, so T_0 → B_3 is carrying and the device is far below the 100 MΩ bias resistor. What I do not have is where the charge neutrality point sits — the brief withholds it, and every later step (the gate map's window, the fixed-D cuts, the fan's density axis) is anchored on it. A single 1D V_bg cut at V_tg = 0 across the whole committed back-gate range sweeps Δn ≈ 5.0 × 10¹² cm⁻² on the geometry prior, which should bracket the CNP unless the intrinsic doping is larger than that.

Read the current channel, not Rxx, this run. sr1 is railed — sens 2 µV against a 2.022 µV reading, fs = 1.01 — so its Rxx number (205 Ω) is a lower bound, not a measurement. sr0 is at fs 0.50 and cannot rail going forward (the drain current only falls as the device approaches the CNP), so the two-terminal conductance dip is the valid CNP locator here. sr1 is still followed and plotted so the sensitivity fix shows up the moment it lands. Ask is out to the operator: sr1 sens → 1 mV, and τ → 0.1 s on sr0+sr1.

Dwell is compliant, not bent. τ = 0.3 s at 24 dB/oct ⇒ 7τ = 2.1 s, which is what delay is set to. That is the whole reason the τ ask matters: it prices this 133-point cut at ~5 min and the coarse gate map at ~2 h.

Preconditions asserted before anything moves: thermometry worker live (age + cadence, so a frozen logfile cannot pass), T_sample in the base window, |B| ≤ 0.02 T (this cell never touches the magnet), V_si = 0 (silent inherited axis), and — the one that would silently waste the run — both Keithley source outputs ON, since a gate set into a disabled output is inert and would look like a featureless trace.

Checkpoint: first rows watched live for railing, a dead channel, or leakage excess; the run is short enough that the periodic checkpoint is the completion read.

ana 13

Read: the device is alive and well behaved, and the CNP sits at V_bg ≈ −0.20 V at V_tg = 0 — a clean, symmetric dip in the drain current. Leakage is clean: both gate currents are flat and voltage-independent (TG −100 pA, BG +25 pA offsets on a 1.05 µA range at NPLC 1, i.e. offset and read noise, not leakage). The ~100 pA spikes appear simultaneously on both independent Keithleys, so they are pickup or a read collision — real gate leakage cannot be common-mode across two separate instruments.

Two things this run taught that changed the plan:

  1. sr1 clipped over 30 % of the sweep (2 µV full scale, pinned above 218 Ω), so the CNP peak height is unmeasured here. Run 1 repeats the cut re-ranged.
  1. The drain current cannot substitute for Rxx. I had planned to read the CNP off sr0, but with a 100 MΩ bias resistor defining the current, dI/I = −dR₂ₜ/10⁸: a channel going 100 Ω → 100 kΩ moves the current by 0.1 %. The dip is visible (0.7 %), but that corresponds to ~0.7 MΩ of R₂ₜ change, which — against a four-terminal Rxx of ~100 Ω — means it is the contacts, not the channel, doing the moving (~0.4 MΩ per contact, roughly doubling through the CNP). Under a high-impedance current bias the drain current is a contact-resistance probe, not a channel probe.
What Pass A extracted here (1 claim)

The agent concluded that under this high-impedance current bias, the drain current cannot serve as a charge-neutrality locator, because a ~100 megohm bias resistor makes the current only weakly sensitive to channel resistance until the channel resistance approaches the bias resistor's own value.

  • Concluded that under this high-impedance current bias, the drain current cannot serve as a charge-neutrality locator.
  • Reason: a ~100 MOhm bias resistor makes the current only weakly sensitive to channel resistance until the channel resistance approaches the bias resistor's own value.

HERA — P1b: re-range sr1, re-run the back-gate cut measure 36–37

measure 36

HERA — P1b: re-range sr1, re-run the back-gate cut

12:20 · bg-cut: sr1 sens 2uV->1mV + sr0/sr1 tau 0.3->0.1 s (operator-authorized), then 1D V_bg +2.00 to -1.30 V, 133 pts @ 25 mV, V_tg=0, V_si=0, B=0, T=base, delay 0.7 s (7 tau) · ETA ~12:24 (≈4 min)

Plan step P1 (second pass). Run 0 passed Gate C but clipped the one channel that matters. This cell fixes the acquisition and repeats the cut; it costs ~2.5 min and gates the ~45 min map that follows, so it runs first.

What run 0 established. The drain current traces a clean, symmetric dip centred at V_bg = −0.200 V at V_tg = 0 — that is the CNP, and on the geometry prior it puts the intrinsic doping at n_offset ≈ +3.0 × 10¹¹ cm⁻² (slightly electron-doped) with the CNP sitting at D/ε₀ ≈ +0.027 V/nm, i.e. essentially zero field. Leakage is clean: both gate currents are flat and voltage-independent (TG −100 pA, BG +25 pA offsets), and the ~100 pA spikes appear simultaneously on both independent gates, which is pickup or a read collision, not leakage — real gate leakage cannot be common-mode across two separate Keithleys.

Why sr1 must be re-ranged. Rxx clipped at 218 Ω (fs 1.09) over 30 % of the sweep, so the CNP peak height is unmeasured. The drain current cannot substitute: the 100 MΩ bias resistor defines the current, so a device going 100 Ω → 100 kΩ moves I by ~0.1 %. New sensitivity 1 mV = 100 kΩ of Rxx headroom at 10 nA bias, which covers a flat-band CNP; the metallic end (65 Ω, 0.65 µV) sits 60 dB down, well inside an SR830's reserve.

Why τ drops to 0.1 s. Compliant dwell is 7τ, so 0.3 s costs 2.1 s/pt and prices the coarse map at ~1.9 h; 0.1 s costs 0.7 s/pt and prices it at ~45 min. At the 13.777 Hz drive a 100 ms 24 dB/oct filter still puts 2f (27.6 Hz) about 99 dB down. It is set on sr0 as well as sr1 — the dwell is gated by the slowest channel, so re-ranging only sr1 would buy nothing. Both are instrument-configuration writes on lock-in inputs; no validator, gate limit, field cap or T cap is touched.

One systematic this run will let me size. R₂ₜ off-CNP is ~0.75 MΩ against a four-terminal Rxx of ~100 Ω, so the contacts dominate the two-terminal resistance (~0.4 MΩ each), and they roughly double through the CNP. That matters because the SR830 input is 10 MΩ: ~0.8 MΩ of series probe resistance divides Vxx down by ~7 %, and worse if the probe contacts go strongly resistive at the CNP. So absolute Rxx carries a systematic that grows near the CNP. sr1_Y (the quadrature) is followed and plotted precisely so I can watch for the phase drift that would flag it.

Reverse direction (+2.00 → −1.30 V): starts where run 0 left the gate, and buys a hysteresis check against run 0 for free.

Checkpoint: first digest rows for clipping and for the new noise floor at the metallic end — if 1 mV proves too coarse there, that shows up immediately and costs 2 min, not 45.

Run 1 — bg-cut: same cut, sr1 re-ranged to 1 mV

Why / what we're testing: run 0 clipped the only channel that measures the channel. This repeats the identical cut with sr1 at 1 mV (100 kΩ of Rxx headroom at 10 nA) and τ dropped 0.3 → 0.1 s on both sr0 and sr1, to (a) measure the CNP peak height without clipping and (b) set the Rxx scale for the gate map. τ = 0.1 s at 24 dB/oct still puts 2f (27.6 Hz) ~99 dB down at the 13.777 Hz drive, and the compliant dwell falls 2.1 s → 0.7 s per point — the reason the map costs ~34 min and not ~1.9 h.

# Run 1 read: CNP peak height, hysteresis vs run 0, and whether the point-to-point
# wiggle is noise or reproducible structure.
def _rxx(g):
    mc = g.meta["measurement_config"]
    v = g.col("k_2400_bg_volt")
# Run 1 read: CNP peak height, hysteresis vs run 0, and whether the point-to-point
# wiggle is noise or reproducible structure.
def _rxx(g):
    mc = g.meta["measurement_config"]
    v = g.col("k_2400_bg_volt")
    I = g.col("sr0_X") / mc["sr0_gain"]
    return v, I, g.col("sr1_X") / I, g.col("sr1_Y") / I   # R from MEASURED current

v0, I0, R0, _ = _rxx(g0)
v1, I1, R1, Q1 = _rxx(g1)
o1 = np.argsort(v1)

k1 = int(np.argmax(R1))
print(f"CNP from Rxx peak (run 1): V_bg = {v1[k1]:+.4f} V,  Rxx_peak = {R1[k1]:.1f} ohm")
print(f"CNP from I dip    (run 0): V_bg = {v0[int(np.argmin(np.abs(I0)))]:+.4f} V")
print(f"hysteresis between sweep directions: "
      f"{abs(v1[int(np.argmin(np.abs(I1)))] - v0[int(np.argmin(np.abs(I0)))]) * 1e3:.0f} mV "
      f"(one 25 mV grid step -> negligible gate charging)")

# Runs 0 and 1 are independent sweeps in opposite directions with different tau AND
# different sensitivity, so comparing them separates noise from structure. For pure white
# noise the run-to-run rms difference equals hypot(sigma0, sigma1); any excess is real.
un = v0 > 0.6                                   # run-0 unclipped, electron side
R1i = np.interp(v0[un], v1[o1], R1[o1])
sig0 = np.std(np.diff(R0[un])) / np.sqrt(2)     # successive differences -> per-point sigma
sig1 = np.std(np.diff(R1i)) / np.sqrt(2)
obs = np.std(R0[un] - R1i)
exc = np.sqrt(max(obs ** 2 - sig0 ** 2 - sig1 ** 2, 0.0))
mean = R0[un].mean()

      f"run1 {sig1:.2f} ohm ({100 * sig1 / mean:.1f} %)")
print(f"run-to-run rms diff : observed {obs:.2f} ohm vs {np.hypot(sig0, sig1):.2f} ohm "
      f"expected for pure independent noise")
print(f"reproducible excess : {exc:.2f} ohm ({100 * exc / mean:.1f} %)  ->  the wiggle is "

print(f"sigma in volts      : {sig1 * 10e-9 * 1e9:.0f} nV  ->  "

ana 17

Read: the CNP is at V_bg = −0.250 V at V_tg = 0, and the neutrality-point resistance there is Rxx = 297 Ω. On the geometry prior that anchors the session's gate calibration: n_offset ≈ +3.8 × 10¹¹ cm⁻² (slightly electron-doped as grown), the CNP line is V_bg = −1.158·V_tg − 0.250, and this particular crossing sits at D/ε₀ = +0.034 V/nm — effectively zero displacement field. So 297 Ω is the D ≈ 0 reference the whole stacking argument is measured against.

Supporting reads:

  • Hysteresis is 50 mV, one grid step, between sweeps in opposite directions. The gates are not charging up, so map rows taken minutes apart are comparable.
  • The point-to-point wiggle is noise, not structure. Per-point σ is 2.2 Ω (run 0) and 3.2 Ω (run 1); the observed run-to-run rms difference of 4.5 Ω is very close to the 3.8 Ω that pure independent noise predicts, leaving only ~2 Ω (≈2 %) of reproducible excess. In volts that σ is ~32 nV, i.e. ~36 nV/√Hz input-referred at the 0.78 Hz ENBW — exactly SR830 1/f noise at 13.8 Hz. So the measurement is instrument-noise-limited and not drifting, and features below ~3 % are not to be believed. (An earlier version of this cell called the wiggles reproducible structure; comparing them properly against the noise-only prediction shows that was wrong.)
  • A double-peaked neutrality region — peaks at V_bg = −0.25 V (297 Ω) and ≈ +0.15 V (272 Ω) with a 35 % dip to 194 Ω between them. That is an order of magnitude above the noise floor, so it is real; but it is seen in one sweep only, because run 0 clipped across exactly this region. The map's 35 independent CNP crossings are the test. If it persists it means either two regions of slightly different doping between the B_1–B_2 probes, or genuine multi-band structure at neutrality — and the latter would itself be a stacking clue, since a Bernal tetralayer carries two bilayer-like bands with different masses.

Caveat carried forward: the device card gives no Hall-bar geometry, so these ohms are not ohms-per-square — 297 Ω is ~1/20 of a graphene minimum-conductivity square, which almost certainly means the B_1–B_2 probes span well under one square rather than that the sheet is anomalously conducting. Every claim in the final call therefore rests on relative changes. Probe loading pushes the same way: R₂ₜ implies ~0.4 MΩ contacts against the SR830's 10 MΩ input, so absolute Rxx reads a few per cent low, and the quadrature (|Y/X| ≤ 0.2) is the tell if that worsens near a gapped CNP.

What Pass A extracted here (6 claims)

The agent changed the Rxx lock-in's sensitivity from 2 microvolt (clipping) to 1 millivolt and lowered the time constant on both lock-ins from 0.3 s to 0.1 s, cutting the compliant per-point dwell from ~2.1 s to ~0.7 s for every subsequent sweep.

The repeat back-gate liveness cut was swept in reverse (from the positive end back down) relative to the first pass, letting the agent get a hysteresis check between the two sweeps at no extra cost.

The agent inferred that two-terminal contact resistance, not the channel, dominates the drain-current dip seen near neutrality, estimating roughly 0.4 megohm of resistance per contact that roughly doubles through the neutrality point.

  • Estimated roughly 0.4 MOhm of resistance per contact.
  • This contact resistance roughly doubles through the neutrality point.

The agent flagged a double-peaked structure near neutrality seen in one of the two back-gate cuts as ambiguous, proposing it reflects either two slightly differently doped regions between the voltage probes or genuine multi-band structure at neutrality, and deferred judgment to the upcoming gate map's many neutrality crossings.

HERA — P2: coarse (n, D) gate map — the primary stacking discriminator measure 38–39

measure 38

HERA — P2: coarse (n, D) gate map — the primary stacking discriminator

12:25 · gate-map: 2D megasweep, slow V_bg -1.30 to +0.40 V x35 @ 50 mV, fast V_tg -0.30 to +1.00 V x66 @ 20 mV, 2310 pts, V_si=0, B=0, T=base, fast/slow delay 0.7 s; CNP line spans D/eps0 +0.320 to -0.067 V/nm · ETA ~13:07 (≈42 min)

Plan step P2. This is the measurement the call rests on. ABAB, ABCA and ABCB differ most cheaply in what a displacement field does to the charge-neutral point: a Bernal tetralayer is a band-overlapped semimetal that stays conducting under D; a rhombohedral one opens a large single-particle gap that grows with |D| and drives R_CNP up by orders of magnitude; a mixed ABCB stack gaps too, but — lacking inversion symmetry — not symmetrically about D = 0. One map answers all three.

What P1 already fixed. Run 1 puts the CNP at V_bg = −0.250 V at V_tg = 0, i.e. n_offset ≈ +3.8 × 10¹¹ cm⁻² and a crossing at D/ε₀ ≈ +0.034 V/nm — effectively zero field. So the CNP line is V_bg = −1.158·V_tg − 0.250 on the geometry prior, and the peak Rxx there is 297 Ω. Hysteresis between the up- and down-sweeps is 50 mV, one grid step, so the gates are not charging up on us.

Why the slow axis stops at +0.400 V, not +2.000 V. The CNP line leaves the top-gate box at V_bg = +0.097 V. Every row above that is pure electron doping and crosses no neutrality point, so it carries no stacking information — it would have been 25 of 45 rows and ~25 min of fridge time for nothing. Spending that budget on resolution instead gives 50 mV rows over the window that matters: ~29 distinct D values along the CNP line, from D/ε₀ = +0.320 V/nm down to −0.067 V/nm.

The one-sided-D problem, stated up front. That window is the plan's flagged risk made concrete. Negative D at neutrality requires V_tg < 0, and the provided top-gate limit stops at −0.3 V — which is an operating limit I am not permitted to probe or extend. So +D has a five-fold longer lever arm than −D. This does not kill the ABCB test: the inversion-symmetry question is where the R_CNP maximum sits, and a symmetric ±0.067 V/nm window straddling D = 0 is available to answer it. It does mean any ABCB verdict rests on a short lever arm and must be hedged accordingly.

Reading it. Rxx is Vxx / I_measured, and resistance_grids uses the measured drain current, so the number stays honest if the current bias sags into a resistive device. sr1 at 1 mV covers up to 100 kΩ; if R_CNP climbs past that at high D, the clipping is itself the ABCA/ABCB signature and I will re-range and re-cut rather than trust the rail.

Absolute-vs-relative caveat, recorded now. The device card gives no Hall-bar geometry, so Rxx in ohms cannot be converted to R per square — 297 Ω is only ~1/20 of a graphene minimum-conductivity square, which almost certainly means the B_1–B_2 probes span well under one square, not that the sheet is anomalously conducting. Every claim in the final call therefore rests on relative changes (R_CNP(D)/R_CNP(0), activation, SdH periods), never on an absolute R per square. Probe loading pushes the same way: R₂ₜ says the probe contacts are ~0.4 MΩ against the SR830's 10 MΩ input, so absolute Rxx reads ~7–10 % low, and the quadrature (|Y/X| ≤ 0.2, followed and plotted) is the tell if that worsens.

Cost ~34 min of measurement (2310 pts at the run-1 calibrated 0.855 s/pt, plus 1.6 s of flyback per row); priced at 42 min to leave margin.

Checkpoints, both stated here: first two rows read for clipping, a dead channel, or leakage excess — the cheapest kill is in the first minute. Then per-row digests, with the real decision at row ~20, by which point the CNP line has been crossed from D = +0.32 down through +0.05 V/nm. If R_CNP is climbing steeply across those rows the answer is already rhombohedral-like and the rest of the session goes to activation; if it is flat at a few hundred ohms, it is Bernal-like and the Landau fan becomes the confirming measurement.

assert sr0.time_constant() == 0.1 and sr1.time_constant() == 0.1, "tau is not 0.1 s — dwell would be wrong"
assert sr1.sensitivity() == 1e-3, "sr1 sensitivity is not 1 mV — Rxx range would be wrong"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the map
DATA_DIR = os.path.join(main_dir, "data")
VTG = spoints(-0.30, 1.00, 66)    # fast, 20 mV steps  (small span -> cheap flyback)
VBG = spoints(-1.30, 0.40, 35)    # slow, 50 mV steps  (starts where run 1 ended)
FAST_DELAY = 0.7                  # 7*tau at tau = 0.1 s — compliant
SLOW_DELAY = 0.7

# sanity: every point of this grid must sit inside the committed validators
assert VTG.min() >= -0.3 and VTG.max() <= 1.0, "fast axis outside the TG operating limit"
assert VBG.min() >= -1.3 and VBG.max() <= 2.0, "slow axis outside the BG operating limit"

meas_config["comments"] = ("gate-map — coarse (n, D) map at B = 0, base T; the CNP line runs "
                           "diagonally across this window and R_CNP(D) is the primary "
                           "ABAB / ABCA / ABCB discriminator")
meas_config["sample_temperature:"] = _Ts
meas_config["Si (V)"] = _Vsi

s = sweep.AsyncStation(meas_config, basedir=DATA_DIR)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.Y).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.Y)
s.fp(k_2400_tg.curr).fp(k_2400_bg.curr).fp(T_sample)
s.add_comment("gate-map")
s.add_comment(
    "2D megasweep | slow V_bg -1.300 -> +0.400 V, 35 rows @ 50 mV | "
    "fast V_tg -0.300 -> +1.000 V, 66 pts @ 20 mV | 2310 pts | "
    "V_si = 0.000 V | B = 0 T | T = base (~1.17 K) | "
    "fast_delay 0.7 s = 7*tau (tau 0.1 s, 24 dB/oct), slow_delay 0.7 s | "
    "I_bias 10.0 nA (1.0 V / 100 MOhm @ 13.777 Hz) | "
    "sr0 = drain current T_0 -> B_3, Ithaco -1e6, sens 20 mV | "
    "sr1 = Vxx B_1-B_2, sens 1 mV | "
    "window chosen so the CNP line is inside it: from run 1 the CNP sits at "
    "V_bg = -0.250 V when V_tg = 0, so the line is V_bg = -1.158*V_tg - 0.250 and it "
    "leaves the TG box at V_bg = +0.097 — rows above ~+0.1 V never cross the CNP, "
    "which is why the slow axis stops at +0.400 instead of +2.000 (that upper half "
    "is pure electron doping and would have cost ~25 min for no stacking information)"
)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, [sr0.X, sr0.Y, sr1.X, sr1.Y,
                   k_2400_tg.curr, k_2400_bg.curr, T_sample])
s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.X, k_bg.volt)      # the map itself, live

res = s.megasweep(k_bg.volt, VBG, k_tg.volt, VTG,
                  slow_delay=SLOW_DELAY, fast_delay=FAST_DELAY, init_delay=True)
print(f"\nrun id = {res.id}   {res.datapath}")
print(f"post: V_bg = {k_bg.volt():+.4f} V   V_tg = {k_tg.volt():+.4f} V   "
      f"T_sample = {T_sample():.3f} K   B = {magnet.field():+.4f} T")

What Pass A extracted here (1 claim)

For the coarse gate map, the agent swept the back gate across its full negative range but stopped the positive side at +0.40 V, well short of the card limit, once it determined the charge-neutrality line exits the accessible top-gate window there, and put the freed sweep budget into finer step resolution instead.

  • For the coarse gate map, swept the back gate across its full negative range.
  • Stopped the positive side at +0.40 V, well short of the card limit.
  • Reason: determined the charge-neutrality line exits the accessible top-gate window there.
  • Put the freed sweep budget into finer step resolution instead.

HERA — P2 re-run: gate map without the 2D live plot (run 2 post-mortem)

12:28 · gate-map RE-RUN (run 2 died at pt 3, plotter BrokenPipeError): identical 2D megasweep, slow V_bg -1.30 to +0.40 V x35 @ 50 mV, fast V_tg -0.30 to +1.00 V x66 @ 20 mV, 2310 pts, B=0, T=base, delay 0.7 s; 2D live plot removed · ETA ~13:10 (≈42 min)

Run 2 died at point 3 of 2310 with BrokenPipeError: [WinError 232] raised from Plotter.add_point — the live-plot subprocess fell over and took the sweep down with it. Preconditions had all passed (T 1.170 K, B +0.0063 T, V_si 0, both Keithley outputs on, τ 0.1 s, sr1 1 mV) and the station had already printed its 27m 21s estimate, so nothing about the device, the gates or the measurement is implicated.

Cause. The extra s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.X, k_bg.volt) I added for a live map. In sweep/plot.py the mesh branch runs ax.clear() → griddata(...) → pcolormesh(...) on every measured point, re-interpolating the entire accumulated dataset each time — O(N²) work in the child process — and it is degenerate early on, when the slow axis still holds a single unique value. Runs 0 and 1 plotted seven 1D channels with no z and both completed cleanly, which isolates the 2D call as the difference.

Fix: drop the 2D live plot, change nothing else. This is no loss. The rig card already warns that plot.png is the live monitor and not the measurement for rastered or co-swept maps — the map has to be re-formed from the TSV with fan_grids / resistance_grids regardless, which is what the analysis does. The seven per-channel 1D plots stay, so the operator still sees every followed value live; that is the exact configuration already proven over two runs.

No measurement parameter changed — same window, same steps, same delays, same channels. Run 2's 3-point stub stays on disk as the record of the failure.

Lesson recorded in session_notes.md: never give a long megasweep a 2D live plot on this stack; a monitor crash must not be able to destroy a 34-minute measurement. The cheap insurance is that hera-watch caught it within a minute — it reported partial: 3/2310 and exited instead of hanging, so the cost of the failure was ~1 min, not 34.

Run 3 — gate-map: the (n, D) map, and the primary stacking discriminator

Why / what we're testing: ABAB, ABCA and ABCB differ most cheaply in what a displacement field does to charge neutrality. A Bernal (ABAB) tetralayer is a band-overlapped semimetal and stays conducting under D. A rhombohedral (ABCA) one is inversion-symmetric and gapless at D = 0, so a gap opens ∝ |D| and R_CNP has a minimum exactly at D = 0, symmetric either side. A mixed (ABCB) stack has no inversion symmetry, carries a built-in gap at D = 0, and so puts its minimum at finite D. One map answers all three: 35 rows × 66 points, slow V_bg −1.30 → +0.40 V, fast V_tg −0.30 → +1.00 V, B = 0, T = 1.17 K.

The window stops at V_bg = +0.40 rather than the +2.00 limit because the CNP line leaves the top-gate box at V_bg ≈ +0.10 — rows above that cross no neutrality point and carry no stacking information. That budget went into resolution instead: ~30 distinct D values along the CNP line.

(Run 2 was this same measurement and died at point 3 of 2310 with a BrokenPipeError from the live-plot subprocess — sweep/plot.py rebuilds the whole 2D mesh via ax.clear() + griddata + pcolormesh on every point. Run 3 is identical with the 2D live plot removed; the 3-point stub is left on disk as the record.)

# Run 3 read: re-form the fan, extract R_CNP(D) along the CNP line, measure the
# session's c_tg/c_bg from the CNP-line slope, and test inversion symmetry.
#
# Peak extraction is parabolic (sub-step) around argmax; the CNP-line fit uses only
# rows where the ridge is unambiguous (single-peaked, tall) and is then extrapolated
# Run 3 read: re-form the fan, extract R_CNP(D) along the CNP line, measure the
# session's c_tg/c_bg from the CNP-line slope, and test inversion symmetry.
#
# Peak extraction is parabolic (sub-step) around argmax; the CNP-line fit uses only
# rows where the ridge is unambiguous (single-peaked, tall) and is then extrapolated
# into the low-|D| region where the neutrality peak is broad.
fan3 = fan_grids(g3)
rg3 = resistance_grids(fan3)
Vtg3 = fan3.grid("k_2400_tg_volt")
Vbg3 = fan3.slow
R3 = np.abs(rg3.R["sr1"])
nrows, nfast = R3.shape
dv = Vtg3[0, 1] - Vtg3[0, 0]

kpk = np.argmax(R3, axis=1)
Vpk = np.empty(nrows); Rpk = np.empty(nrows)
for i, k in enumerate(kpk):
    if 0 < k < nfast - 1:
        y0, y1, y2 = R3[i, k - 1], R3[i, k], R3[i, k + 1]
        den = y0 - 2 * y1 + y2
        d = np.clip(0.5 * (y0 - y2) / den, -1, 1) if den != 0 else 0.0
        Vpk[i], Rpk[i] = Vtg3[i, k] + d * dv, y1 - 0.25 * (y0 - y2) * d
    else:
        Vpk[i], Rpk[i] = Vtg3[i, k], R3[i, k]
edge = (kpk <= 1) | (kpk >= nfast - 2)

def _npeaks(row, frac=0.80):
    m = row.max()
    return sum(1 for j in range(1, nfast - 1)
               if row[j] > row[j - 1] and row[j] >= row[j + 1] and row[j] > frac * m)

npk = np.array([_npeaks(R3[i]) for i in range(nrows)])
good = (~edge) & (npk == 1) & (Rpk / np.median(R3, axis=1) > 1.6)

A3, cov3 = np.polyfit(Vbg3[good], Vpk[good], 1, cov=True)
slope, icept = A3
sl_err = float(np.sqrt(cov3[0, 0]))
RATIO = -1.0 / slope
RATIO_ERR = sl_err / slope ** 2
print(f"rows: {nrows} total, {(~edge).sum()} interior, {(npk == 1).sum()} single-peaked, "
      f"{good.sum()} used for the CNP-line fit")
print(f"CNP line: V_tg = {slope:+.5f}(+/-{sl_err:.5f})*V_bg {icept:+.5f}")
print(f"  MEASURED c_tg/c_bg = {RATIO:.4f} +/- {RATIO_ERR:.4f}   "
      f"(geometry prior {cal.c_tg/cal.c_bg:.4f}, {100*(RATIO/(cal.c_tg/cal.c_bg)-1):+.1f} %)")

# session calibration: measured RATIO, absolute scale still from the geometry prior
cal_s = GateCalibration(c_tg=cal.c_tg, c_bg=cal.c_tg / RATIO)
D3 = cal_s.displacement_field(Vpk, Vbg3) * 1e-9
use = ~edge
o = np.argsort(D3[use])
Dv, Rv, npv = D3[use][o], Rpk[use][o], npk[use][o]

kmin = int(np.argmin(Rv))
sel = np.abs(Dv - Dv[kmin]) < 0.10
qq = np.polyfit(Dv[sel], np.log10(Rv[sel]), 2)
D_min = -qq[1] / (2 * qq[0])
print(f"\nR_CNP: {Rv.min():.0f} .. {Rv.max():.0f} ohm  ({Rv.max()/Rv.min():.1f}x)")
print(f"D covered: {Dv.min():+.4f} .. {Dv.max():+.4f} V/nm "

print(f"R_CNP MINIMUM: argmin {Dv[kmin]:+.4f}, parabola on log10 R {D_min:+.4f} V/nm "
      f"-> D_min = 0.000 +/- 0.008 V/nm")
for rr, tag in ((RATIO - RATIO_ERR, "-1sig"), (RATIO + RATIO_ERR, "+1sig")):

Read: this is the measurement the stacking call rests on, and it says three things.

1. A displacement field opens a gap — 10.4×. R at neutrality goes from 296 Ω at D ≈ 0 to 3074 Ω at D/ε₀ = +0.31 V/nm, rising steeply through 0.1–0.2 V/nm and then saturating above ~0.23 V/nm. This excludes ABAB. A Bernal tetralayer is a band-overlapped semimetal: displacement field gaps each bilayer-like subband but shifts them relative to one another, so the overlap survives and the CNP stays conducting. A 10× insulating rise is not that.

2. The gap minimum sits at D = 0 — the stack is inversion-symmetric. The R_CNP minimum is at D/ε₀ = 0.000 ± 0.008 V/nm (argmin −0.008, parabolic fit on log R +0.008), and it is robust: pushing the measured c_tg/c_bg by ±1σ moves it by under 0.001 V/nm. Folded about that minimum the two branches lie on top of each other — R(+D)/R(−D) = 1.07, 1.01, 1.03, 0.96 at |ΔD| = 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08 V/nm, against a ~3 % per-point noise floor. This disfavours ABCB, which lacks inversion symmetry: its built-in D = 0 gap is closed by a field of one particular sign, so its R_CNP minimum must sit at finite D. Nothing here is displaced by more than 0.008 V/nm out of a 0.39 V/nm range.

Together: ABCA (rhombohedral).

3. The session's own gate calibration. The CNP-line slope over 26 unambiguous rows gives c_tg/c_bg = 1.2737 ± 0.0470, ~10 % above the geometry prior's 1.1579 — within about 2σ, but the measured value is what every subsequent cell uses to define the D = 0 line. The absolute scale still rests on the prior; the Landau fan is what will fix that.

Three honest limits on this evidence.

  • The −D lever arm is only 0.26 of +D. Negative D at neutrality needs V_tg < 0, and the provided top-gate limit stops at −0.3 V — an operating limit the session brief bans me from probing. So symmetry is demonstrated over |D| ≤ 0.08 V/nm, not over the full range. An ABCB asymmetry that only develops beyond that would not be visible here.
  • Seven rows have a double-peaked neutrality region, all at low |D| — the same structure run 1 showed. Those rows sit squarely in the window used for the symmetry test. It is most likely two areas of slightly different doping between the B_1–B_2 probes; that the branches still fold cleanly argues it is not corrupting the result, but it is the reason the peak extraction is parabolic and the line fit uses only single-peaked rows.
  • The saturation above 0.23 V/nm is not what a clean growing gap does. A single-particle gap should keep driving R up exponentially. A plateau at ~3 kΩ points to a parallel conduction path or disorder-induced in-gap states setting a floor — and it means the activation measurement, not R itself, is the honest route to a gap in meV.

The agent concluded that the ~10x, displacement-field-driven rise in neutrality-point resistance rules out a band-overlapped semimetallic (Bernal-type) stacking, since such a stacking's overlapping bands should keep the neutrality point conducting under displacement field.

  • Reasoning: such a stacking's overlapping bands should keep the neutrality point conducting under displacement field.

The agent inferred that the neutrality-resistance minimum sitting at zero displacement field, with the two field-sign branches folding onto each other, demonstrates inversion symmetry of the stack and disfavors a stacking that lacks inversion symmetry, whose built-in gap would displace the minimum to finite field.

HERA — P4: Landau fan at D = 0 — independent test of the band structure measure 42–43

measure 42

HERA — P4: Landau fan at D = 0 — independent test of the band structure

13:08 · landau-fan: 2D multimegasweep, slow magnet.field 0.75 to 6.0 T x40 uniform in 1/B, fast co-swept (V_tg,V_bg) along measured D=0 line (V_bg=1.2737*V_tg), V_tg -0.30 to +0.60 V x46 @ 20 mV, n=-1.04 to +2.10e12 cm-2, 1840 pts, T=base, delay 0.7/1.0 s · ETA ~14:38 (≈1h30m)

Plan step P4. The gate map has taken the call a long way: R at neutrality rises 10.4× with displacement field (296 Ω → 3074 Ω), and its minimum sits at D/ε₀ = 0.000 ± 0.008 V/nm with the two branches symmetric to within 7 % out to |D| = 0.08 V/nm. That excludes ABAB (a band-overlapped semimetal would not gap like that) and disfavours ABCB (which, lacking inversion symmetry, must put its minimum at finite D). The remaining hypothesis is ABCA.

Everything above, though, is one measurement of one quantity. This fan is an independent test, of the band structure rather than the gap:

  • Landau-level degeneracy. A rhombohedral N-layer stack carries an N-fold orbitally-degenerate zero-energy level; for tetralayer ABCA that is 4 × 4 (spin×valley) = 16 states, so the first flanking gaps fall at ν = ±8. A Bernal tetralayer decomposes into two bilayer-like sets whose levels arrive at different fields, giving a visibly different sequence. Counting filling factors settles it on band structure alone.
  • Fermi-pocket count. One SdH tone carrying the full Onsager frequency ⇒ a single quartic band (ABCA); two tones splitting it ⇒ two pockets (ABAB/ABCB).
  • The first absolute density calibration. Every number so far rests on the geometry prior for c_tg. LL slopes give dn/dB = νe/h directly, which either confirms that prior or corrects it. Note the map already moved the ratio: measured c_tg/c_bg = 1.2737 ± 0.0470 against the prior's 1.1579, and this cell uses the measured value to define the D = 0 line, not the prior.

Design. Fast axis is density along the measured D = 0 line (V_bg = 1.2737·V_tg), n = −1.04 → +2.10 × 10¹² cm⁻² with the CNP at V_tg = −0.003, so the fan is centred on neutrality and covers both carrier signs. Slow axis is field on a 1/B-uniform grid (field_invB), which is what sdh_fft wants — no resampling, and it naturally puts more rows at low field where the levels converge. D = 0 is chosen deliberately: it is the symmetric point, so the band structure is seen unperturbed.

magnet.field is followed per point because the rig card is explicit that this supply's setpoint is not readable as field — only the measured current is truth.

Cost ~1 h 15 m: 5 min to reach 0.75 T, ~38 min of ramping spread across the 40 rows (the magnet's fixed 0.137 T/min is the floor and dominates), ~28 min of measurement, ~2 min of flyback. Priced at 1 h 30 m. Field is the expensive, one-way axis, so this runs upward once and does not re-traverse — the session's remaining field need after this is the ramp back to zero.

Checkpoints: first row read for clipping and leakage (the gates sit at new values here); then per-row digests, with the decision at row ~10 (B ≈ 1.2 T) — if no oscillatory structure is developing by ~2 T I will reconsider whether the mobility supports a fan at all rather than spend the full hour. Ceiling is 6 T, not the 10 T session cap, precisely because the ramp is the cost: 6 T already puts ν = ±8 comfortably inside the density window, and every extra tesla is ~7 min each way.

Run 4 — landau-fan: band structure at D = 0, and a correction

Why / what we're testing: the gate map settled the call on gap physics. This is an independent look at the band structure — 40 field rows (0.75 → 6 T, uniform in 1/B) × 46 densities co-swept along the session-measured D = 0 line, n = −1.05 → +2.09 × 10¹² cm⁻² with the CNP at V_tg = −0.003.

Correction to the proposing cell. When I launched this run I claimed the Landau-level degeneracy would separate ABCA from ABAB — that a rhombohedral tetralayer's 4-fold orbital zero level (16 states, first gaps at ν = ±8) would look different from a Bernal one. That is wrong, and I retract it. ABAB tetralayer decomposes into two effective bilayers, each carrying a 2-fold orbital zero level × 4 spin/valley = 8 states, and both sit at exactly E = 0 — so ABAB also has 16 zero-energy states. The zero-LL degeneracy is 4N for N layers regardless of stacking: it counts layers, not stacking order. The measure notebook is append-only so the original claim stands there; this is the corrected record.

What this run can still do is count Fermi pockets, which does discriminate: a rhombohedral stack has one quartic band at D = 0, a Bernal tetralayer has two bilayer-like bands both crossing E_F and therefore two SdH tones.

Read: the fan is textbook — a symmetric ladder of Rxx minima radiating from n = 0, and a ν = 0 insulating wedge that widens with field until, at 6 T, Rxx at neutrality reaches 109 kΩ (clipping sr1) with the drain current sagging to 6.4 nA, i.e. R₂ₜ ≈ 55 MΩ. Three things come out of it, and one thing deliberately does not.

1. One Fermi pocket — and this is the α-independent result. The SdH spectrum carries a single tone whose frequency is proportional to n through the origin (r = 0.99), sitting at ~0.85× the full Onsager frequency on the assumed density scale. The other spectral peaks (4.2, 9.7, 9.1, 2.6, 8.4, 4.6 T as n increases) show no trend with density and are FFT sidelobes. This matters because two Fermi pockets would produce two tones that BOTH scale linearly with n at a fixed ratio — that statement needs no calibration at all. A Bernal tetralayer at D = 0 has two bilayer-like bands both crossing E_F and would show exactly that; a rhombohedral one has a single quartic band and shows what we see. This is the fan's contribution to the stacking call, and it points to ABCA.

2. A uniform Landau ladder, spacing Δν = 4.665 on the assumed density scale, with lines resolved out to the tenth on the electron side.

3. Following magnet.field per point was necessary. The measured field sits +6.5 mT above the setpoint with ~2 mT of within-row spread — ~0.9 % at 0.75 T, which would have propagated straight into every extracted frequency. (An early version of this analysis read the setpoint column by mistake: magnet_field appears twice, and FanGrids.grid() silently resolves duplicates to the first occurrence. The giveaway was a suspiciously perfect |cmd − meas| = 0.0 mT.)

What this run does NOT establish: the absolute density scale, or the degeneracy. Both the SdH frequency (f = n_true·h/g·e) and the ladder spacing depend only on the product α·g, where α = n_assumed/n_true is the error in the absolute gate capacitance. Both routes agree — α·g ≈ 4.7 — and both are blind to the split. Separating them needs a density measurement independent of degeneracy, i.e. the Hall resistance n = B/(e·R_xy), and this cooldown has no Hall pair: sr2 and sr3 are n.c. in the provided contact configuration, so R_xy cannot be formed. That is a wiring limitation, not an analysis one.

If one assumes the standard 4-fold spin–valley degeneracy — which holds for the LLs above the zero level in every candidate stacking — then α = 1.17 and c_tg = 2.40 mF/m², an 11.1 nm equivalent hBN thickness at κ = 3 against the card's 9.5 nm. That is a believable 17 % geometry error, and it is the reading I adopt; but it is an assumption, and every absolute density in this session inherits it. Nothing in the stacking call depends on it — the gate map's evidence is a ratio (10.4×) and a symmetry point (D = 0), and the fan's evidence is a tone count.

When proposing the Landau fan, the agent claimed that a rhombohedral four-layer stack's Landau-level degeneracy (a single 16-fold-degenerate zero-energy level, giving first flanking gaps at filling factor +/-8) would look visibly different from a Bernal-stacked four-layer's Landau-level sequence, and that counting filling factors alone would settle the stacking order.

HERA — P4b: SdH trace measured through the ramp down

14:22 · sdh-downsweep: 2D multimegasweep, slow magnet.field 6.0 to 0.5 T x100 DESCENDING uniform in 1/B, fast 5 fixed densities on D=0 line (n = -0.8/0.5/1.0/1.5/2.0 e12 cm-2), 500 pts, T=base; FFT res 0.55 T, Nyquist 27.3 T · ETA ~15:22 (≈1h)

Plan step P4b. The activation ladder (P5) must be run at zero field, so the 6 T → 0 ramp is unavoidable — 40 minutes of the magnet's fixed 0.137 T/min. Measuring through it costs about 13 minutes extra and turns dead time into the session's highest-resolution SdH dataset. That is the whole justification for this cell.

Why the fan alone is not enough for the pocket count. Run 4's 1/B record (0.75 → 6 T, 40 rows) gives an FFT resolution of 0.86 T but a Nyquist frequency of only ~17 T, while the Onsager frequency at the top of its density window (n = 2.09 × 10¹² cm⁻²) is 21.6 T — those columns alias, and an aliased tone is worse than no tone. This sweep uses 100 field points over a longer 1/B baseline (0.5 → 6 T): resolution 0.55 T, Nyquist 27.3 T, comfortably above every Onsager frequency in play. The fan is the right instrument for the Landau-level sequence; this is the right one for counting tones.

Design. Five fixed densities on the session-measured D = 0 line (n = −0.80, +0.50, +1.00, +1.50, +2.00 × 10¹² cm⁻²), verified to sit at D/ε₀ = 0.000 exactly and inside the committed gate box. Field descends on a field_invB grid so sdh_fft needs no resampling. One tone carrying the full Onsager value means a single Fermi pocket (ABCA); two tones splitting it means two pockets (ABAB/ABCB). Because the five densities span a 4× range, the tones must also scale linearly with n — that is a much stronger check than any single column, and it is what would expose a spurious peak.

magnet.field is followed per point, which run 4 proved is not optional: the measured field sits +6.5 mT above the setpoint with ~2 mT of within-row spread, ~0.9 % at 0.75 T, and that would propagate directly into the extracted frequencies.

Sensitivity is deliberately left at 1 mV. These are finite-density columns where Rxx stays modest; the n = +0.50 column sits at ν ≈ 3.4 at 6 T and may clip near its peaks, which the analysis masks. Coarsening the range to protect it would destroy the SdH minima — run 4 showed those reaching 0–6 Ω, and the minima are half the signal.

Ends at 0.5 T, not 0: a short bare ramp then takes the magnet to zero for the ladder, which is cheaper than measuring the last half-tesla where there is no SdH left to see.

Checkpoints: first rows for clipping and for the current sag (at 6 T the drain current was already down to 6.4 nA at neutrality — these columns are away from it and should sit near 9.9 nA); then per-row digests. Priced at 1 h.

Run 5 — sdh-downsweep: the definitive Fermi-pocket count

Why / what we're testing: the activation ladder needs zero field, so the 6 T → 0 ramp was unavoidable. Measuring through it cost ~13 min over a bare ramp and bought 100 field points (6 → 0.5 T, uniform in 1/B) at 5 fixed densities on the D = 0 line. The point is resolution: this record gives 0.55 T resolution with Nyquist 27.6 T, against the fan's 0.87 T and 17.3 T — the fan aliased its top densities, this does not.

The test needs no calibration. Two Fermi pockets produce two SdH tones, both proportional to n, whose frequencies sum to the full Onsager value. One pocket produces a single tone carrying all of it. Counting tones that scale with density is independent of the absolute density scale — which matters here, because that scale is exactly what this session cannot pin down independently (no Hall pair is wired).

ana 29

Read: one Fermi pocket. Four of the five densities return exactly one unflagged SdH tone; the fifth (n = +1.99) has all its tones flagged marginal or harmonic and yields none. No density yields two. The two highest-contrast traces — n = +0.99 and +1.49 × 10¹² cm⁻², contrast 19.4 and 8.3 — give f/f_full = 0.835 and 0.834, and a fit through the origin over |n| > 0.9 gives 8.62 T per 10¹² cm⁻² against the 10.34 full-Onsager slope.

That is the discriminating fact, and it needs no calibration. Two Fermi pockets would put the dominant tone near 0.7× the full Onsager value and add a second tone near 0.3×, both scaling linearly with n. Neither appears. A Bernal (ABAB) tetralayer at D = 0 has two bilayer-like bands with different masses, both crossing E_F at any finite density, and would show exactly that two-tone structure. A rhombohedral (ABCA) stack has a single quartic band and shows what we see.

An independent consistency check falls out. Reading the 0.834 ratio as a single 4-fold degenerate pocket gives α = 1.199 for the absolute density scale. The Landau fan's minima ladder — a completely different observable, from run 4 — gave α = 1.166. The two agree to 2.8 %. That does not break the α/g degeneracy (both routes still measure only the product), but it does say the two datasets are describing the same Fermi surface consistently.

Caveats. The two low-|n| traces are unreliable and I am not using them in the fit: n = +0.49 and −0.81 carry too few oscillations over the field range, and their apparent ratios (1.02, 1.36) scatter accordingly. The hole side reaches only −0.81 × 10¹² cm⁻² because the top-gate limit bounds it, so the pocket count is really established on the electron side. And a second pocket much smaller than the first — carrying, say, under 10 % of the carriers — would produce a tone below 1.5 T that the degree-5 background removal would eat; this measurement excludes two comparable pockets, not a small satellite.

HERA — P5: temperature ladder — the activation gap Δ(D) measure 46–47

measure 46

HERA — P5: temperature ladder — the activation gap Δ(D)

15:23 · tladder-cnp: ramp B 0.5 to 0 T, then 7 temperatures (base, 8, 12, 17, 23, 30, 40 K via set_both ratio 0.95); at each, 245-pt co-swept multisweep along the measured CNP line x5 perpendicular V_bg offsets, D/eps0 -0.094 to +0.285 V/nm; one run dir per temperature · ETA ~16:13 (≈50 min)

Plan step P5, and the last measurement of the session. Everything so far says the gap is real and centred at D = 0, but says it in resistance. This says it in meV.

Why this is the measurement that closes the argument. Run 3's R_CNP(D) has one feature that does not look like a cleanly growing single-particle gap: above D/ε₀ ≈ 0.23 V/nm it saturates near 3 kΩ instead of continuing up exponentially. That is the signature of a parallel conduction path or disorder-induced in-gap states putting a floor under the resistance — and if that floor dominates, "R rose 10×" would be a weaker claim than it looks. Thermal activation settles it: fitting R_CNP(T) ∝ exp(Δ/2k_BT) at each D returns a gap in meV whose D-dependence is the physics. ABCA requires Δ(D) growing with |D| and extrapolating to ≈ 0 at D = 0; ABCB requires a finite Δ at D = 0.

It is also the one measurement immune to the unknown geometry. The device card gives no Hall-bar dimensions, so every resistance this session is in ohms, not ohms-per-square, and the geometric prefactor is unknown. Activation is a ratio measurement — the prefactor cancels exactly. So does the ~7–10 % probe-loading systematic, provided it does not itself depend on temperature.

Design. At each temperature, one 245-point co-swept multisweep that walks the session-measured CNP line (V_bg = −1.2737·V_tg − 0.00764) five times at perpendicular V_bg offsets of 0, ±0.05, ±0.10 V, folded into a single path and reshaped to (5, 49) in analysis. The offsets matter: they let R_CNP be taken as the maximum over offsets at each point along the line, so a few-mV drift in the fitted line — or thermal drift of the CNP itself as the sample warms — cannot masquerade as a change in gap. One sweep covers D/ε₀ = −0.094 → +0.285 V/nm, so every temperature yields a complete R_CNP(D) curve in under 4 minutes.

Temperatures: base, then 8, 12, 17, 23, 30, 40 K via set_both(T, ratio=0.95) — the rig-card-sanctioned ratio; any deviation is consent-gated and is not used. Points are accepted on stability, not proximity: the rig card records that the sample loop is untuned, overshoots ~+1.4 K, and recovers only as fast as the bath allows, so waiting for |T − setpoint| to close never converges below ~20 K. T_sample is followed per point, so the Arrhenius fit uses the temperature actually measured, never the setpoint. The ladder starts at 8 K deliberately — the rig's electron temperature is ~8 K, so nothing below that carries independent information.

Field to zero first. Activation must be measured at B = 0 or a Landau gap contaminates Δ. The down-sweep left the magnet at 0.5 T, so this cell owns the last leg down and asserts |B| ≤ 0.05 T after the blocking ramp before any heater is touched.

Ends warm, deliberately. This is the last measurement, and cooling back to base from 40 K is passive and slow (τ ≈ 27 min). Close-out does not require base temperature — it requires the field at zero, the gates at zero, and both heater ranges off.

Cost ~50 min: ~4 min of ramp to zero, then 7 × (settle ~3–4 min + sweep ~4 min). Checkpoints: the printed settle line at each temperature (T and its σ), and each run id as it lands — seven separate run directories, so a failure at any temperature costs one point, not the ladder.

print(f"pre: heater ranges sample={heater.sample_range()} vaporizer={heater.vaporizer_range()}")
print(f"pre: sr0 tau={sr0.time_constant():g}s | sr1 tau={sr1.time_constant():g}s "
      f"sens={sr1.sensitivity():.3g}V")
assert 1.10 <= _Ts <= 1.40, f"T_sample {_Ts} K — ladder must start from base"
assert _B <= 1.0, f"B = {_B} T — expected the down-sweep to have left the magnet near 0.5 T"
assert abs(_Vsi) <= 1e-3, f"V_si = {_Vsi} V, expected 0"
assert bool(k_2400_tg.output()) and bool(k_2400_bg.output()), "Keithley output OFF"
assert sr0.time_constant() == 0.1 and sr1.time_constant() == 0.1, "tau is not 0.1 s"
assert sr1.sensitivity() == 1e-3, "sr1 sensitivity is not 1 mV"

# ---------------------------------------- field to zero FIRST
# Activation must be measured at B = 0: a Landau gap at finite field would contaminate
# Delta. The down-sweep ended at 0.5 T, so this cell owns the last leg to zero.
# magnet.field() BLOCKS through the ramp (~4 min at the fixed 0.137 T/min).
if abs(_B) > 0.02:
    print(f"ramping {_B:+.4f} -> 0.000 T (blocking, ~{abs(_B)/0.137:.1f} min) ...")
    magnet.field(0.0)
_B0 = magnet.field()
print(f"field now {_B0:+.4f} T (measured readback)")
assert abs(_B0) <= 0.05, f"B = {_B0} T after ramp — activation needs zero field"

# ---------------------------------------- the CNP-line patch (measured, run 3)
# CNP line: V_tg = -0.7851*V_bg - 0.0060  =>  V_bg = -1.2737*V_tg - 0.00764
# One co-swept 1D path that walks the line five times, each at a different
# perpendicular offset on V_bg, concatenated into a single multisweep. (V_bg cannot
# be both a megasweep slow axis and half of the co-swept fast axis, so the "2D" patch
# is folded into one path and reshaped to (5, 49) in analysis.)
RATIO = 1.2737
VTG_L = spoints(-0.30, 0.90, 49)                  # 25 mV along the line
VBG_L = -RATIO * VTG_L - 0.00764
OFFS = np.array([-0.10, -0.05, 0.0, 0.05, 0.10])  # perpendicular offsets on V_bg
VTG_ALL = np.tile(VTG_L, len(OFFS))
VBG_ALL = np.concatenate([VBG_L + d for d in OFFS])
assert len(VTG_ALL) == len(VBG_ALL) == len(OFFS) * len(VTG_L)
assert VTG_ALL.min() >= -0.3 and VTG_ALL.max() <= 1.0, "V_tg outside the operating limit"
assert VBG_ALL.min() >= -1.3 and VBG_ALL.max() <= 2.0, "V_bg outside the operating limit"
# D/eps0 along the line ~ 0.3158*V_tg + 0.001  ->  -0.094 .. +0.285 V/nm

T_TARGETS = [None, 8.0, 12.0, 17.0, 23.0, 30.0, 40.0]   # None = base, heaters off
assert max(t for t in T_TARGETS if t) <= 100.0, "target above the session T cap"

DATA_DIR = os.path.join(main_dir, "data")


def hover(target, max_wait=600, poll=20, window=5, stab=0.05):
    """Rig-card hover acceptance: accept on STABILITY, not proximity. The sample loop is
    untuned (+1.4 K overshoot, bath-limited recovery), so waiting for |T-target| to close
    never converges below ~20 K. Returns the settled reading."""
    hist = []
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < max_wait:
        interruptible_sleep(poll)
        hist.append(T_sample())
        if len(hist) >= window:
            w = hist[-window:]
            if float(np.std(w)) < stab:
                print(f"    settled: T = {np.mean(w):.3f} K (sigma {np.std(w):.4f} K over "
                      f"{window * poll} s, target {target} K) after {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
                return float(np.mean(w))
    print(f"    WARNING: no stability within {max_wait} s; last T = {hist[-1]:.3f} K")
    return hist[-1]


results = []
for T_set in T_TARGETS:
    if T_set is None:
        print(f"\n=== base temperature (heaters off) ===")
        T_now = T_sample()
    else:
        print(f"\n=== set_both({T_set}, ratio=0.95) ===")
        heater.set_both(T_set, ratio=0.95)   # ratio 0.95 per rig card; any other value is
                                             # consent-gated and is deliberately not used
        T_now = hover(T_set)
    T_vap = T_vaporizer()
    print(f"    T_sample = {T_now:.3f} K   T_vaporizer = {T_vap:.3f} K")

    meas_config["comments"] = (f"tladder-cnp — CNP-line patch at T_sample ~ {T_now:.2f} K, "
                               f"B = 0; activation gap Delta(D) at charge neutrality")
    meas_config["sample_temperature:"] = T_now
    meas_config["Si (V)"] = dc205.voltage()

    s = sweep.AsyncStation(meas_config, basedir=DATA_DIR)
    s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.Y).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.Y)
    s.fp(k_2400_tg.curr).fp(k_2400_bg.curr).fp(T_sample).fp(T_vaporizer)
    s.add_comment("tladder-cnp")
    s.add_comment(
        f"1D multisweep, co-swept (V_tg, V_bg), 245 pts = 5 offsets x 49 along-line pts "
        f"(reshape to (5, 49) in analysis) | line: V_bg = -1.2737*V_tg - 0.00764 "
        f"(MEASURED CNP line from run 3) | V_tg -0.300 -> +0.900 V @ 25 mV | "
        f"perpendicular V_bg offsets {list(np.round(OFFS, 3))} V so the TRUE Rxx peak is "
        f"captured even if the fitted line drifts; R_CNP(D) = max over offsets per V_tg | "
        f"D/eps0 -0.094 .. +0.285 V/nm | "
        f"T_setpoint = {T_set} K (ratio 0.95), T_sample settled = {T_now:.3f} K, "
        f"T_vaporizer = {T_vap:.3f} K | B = 0 T | V_si = 0.000 V | "
        f"delay 0.7 s = 7*tau (tau 0.1 s, 24 dB/oct) | I_bias 10.0 nA | "
        f"sr0 Ithaco -1e6 sens 20 mV | sr1 sens 1 mV"
    )
    s.plot(k_tg.volt, [sr0.X, sr0.Y, sr1.X, sr1.Y,
                       k_2400_tg.curr, k_2400_bg.curr, T_sample, T_vaporizer])

    res = s.multisweep([k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [VTG_ALL, VBG_ALL], delay=0.7)
    results.append((T_set, T_now, res.id))
    print(f"    run {res.id} written")

print("\n=== ladder complete ===")
for T_set, T_now, rid in results:
    print(f"  setpoint {str(T_set):>6} K -> T_sample {T_now:6.3f} K -> run {rid}")
print(f"post: T_sample = {T_sample():.3f} K  T_vaporizer = {T_vaporizer():.3f} K  "
      f"B = {magnet.field():+.4f} T  V_tg = {k_tg.volt():+.4f}  V_bg = {k_bg.volt():+.4f}")

analysis of this data — Runs 6–12 — tladder-cnp: the activation gap Δ(D) (ana 30–33)
ana 30

Runs 6–12 — tladder-cnp: the activation gap Δ(D)

Why / what we're testing: everything up to here says "the resistance at neutrality rises 10× with displacement field." This says what that rise is, in meV, and — critically — it is the one measurement immune to the unknown Hall-bar geometry, because activation is a ratio.

The specific worry it addresses: run 3's R_CNP(D) saturates above D/ε₀ ≈ 0.23 V/nm instead of continuing up exponentially, which is what a parallel conduction path or disorder-induced in-gap states look like. If such a floor dominated the transport, "R rose 10×" would be a much weaker statement than it appears.

Seven temperatures — base, 8, 12, 17, 23, 30, 40 K via set_both(T, ratio=0.95) — each with a 245-point co-swept sweep walking the measured CNP line five times at perpendicular V_bg offsets, so R_CNP is taken as the maximum over offsets and cannot be spoofed by the line drifting or the CNP moving as the sample warms. Every setpoint settled to within 0.01 K (σ ≈ 0.002 K) in ~140 s. Fits use T ≥ 8 K only: the rig's electron temperature is ~8 K, and the data show it — R_CNP is flat between 1.2 and 8 K.

    print(summarize_run(_g).splitlines()[0], "|",
          f"T = {np.mean(_g.col('T_sample')):.3f} K, {_g.rows} pts")

# Activation gap Delta(D) from the ladder (runs 6-12).
#
# R_CNP at each point along the CNP line is the MAXIMUM over the 5 perpendicular offsets —
# that is what makes it robust to the fitted line drifting, or to the CNP itself moving as
# the sample warms. Then at each D fit  ln R_CNP = ln R0 + Delta/(2 k_B T).
# Activation gap Delta(D) from the ladder (runs 6-12).
#
# R_CNP at each point along the CNP line is the MAXIMUM over the 5 perpendicular offsets —
# that is what makes it robust to the fitted line drifting, or to the CNP itself moving as
# the sample warms. Then at each D fit  ln R_CNP = ln R0 + Delta/(2 k_B T).
#   ABCA (inversion symmetric): Delta minimal at D = 0, growing with |D|
#   ABCB (no inversion)       : Delta minimum displaced to finite D
#   ABAB                      : no activated behaviour at all
# COMPLETENESS GUARD below: the 245-pt path is offset0's 49 pts then offset1's 49, ... so a
# partial run reshaped to (5, npts) silently interleaves offsets and yields plausible
# garbage (caught doing exactly that on run 6 mid-write).
here_dir = Path(file_path).parent
RIDS = list(range(6, 13))
RATIO = 1.2737
cal_s = GateCalibration(c_tg=cal.c_tg, c_bg=cal.c_tg / RATIO)
NOFF = 5

curves = []
for rid in RIDS:
    p = here_dir / "data" / str(rid)
    r = open_run(p)
    _sp = r.meta.get("setpoints")
    _exp = len(_sp[0]) if isinstance(_sp, list) and _sp and isinstance(_sp[0], list) else None
    if (_exp is not None and r.rows != _exp) or r.interrupted:
        print(f"run {rid}: incomplete/interrupted ({r.rows} of {_exp}) — skipped")
        continue
    vtg = r.col("k_2400_tg_volt")
    vbg = r.col("k_2400_bg_volt")
    I = r.col("sr0_X") / r.meta["measurement_config"]["sr0_gain"]
    Vxx = r.col("sr1_X")
    npts = len(vtg) // NOFF
    assert npts * NOFF == len(vtg)
    R = np.abs((Vxx / I).reshape(NOFF, npts))
    vtg_g = vtg.reshape(NOFF, npts)
    vbg_g = vbg.reshape(NOFF, npts)
    k = np.nanargmax(R, axis=0)
    Rc = R[k, np.arange(npts)]
    D = cal_s.displacement_field(vtg_g[0], vbg_g[k, np.arange(npts)]) * 1e-9
    Tm = float(np.nanmean(r.col("T_sample")))
    curves.append((Tm, D, Rc, rid))
    print(f"run {rid}: T = {Tm:6.3f} K   R_CNP {Rc.min():7.1f} .. {Rc.max():8.1f} ohm   "
          f"D {D.min():+.3f}..{D.max():+.3f} V/nm")

curves.sort(key=lambda c: c[0])
Ts = np.array([c[0] for c in curves])
Dgrid = curves[0][1]
Rmat = np.vstack([np.interp(Dgrid, c[1], c[2]) for c in curves])

# The rig's ELECTRON temperature is ~8 K, so sub-8 K points carry no independent
# information — and the data show it: R_CNP is flat between 1.2 and 8 K.
fitm = Ts >= 7.0
print(f"\nfitting over T = {np.round(Ts[fitm], 2)} K (base excluded: electron T ~ 8 K)")
inv2kT = 1.0 / (2 * cst.k * Ts[fitm]) * cst.e * 1e-3
gaps, gerr = [], []
for j in range(len(Dgrid)):
    y = np.log(np.maximum(Rmat[fitm, j], 1e-3))
    A = np.vstack([inv2kT, np.ones_like(inv2kT)]).T
    coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, y, rcond=None)
    resid = y - A @ coef
    s2 = float(resid @ resid) / max(len(y) - 2, 1)
    gaps.append(coef[0])
    gerr.append(float(np.sqrt((s2 * np.linalg.inv(A.T @ A))[0, 0])))
gaps, gerr = np.array(gaps), np.array(gerr)

print(f"\n{'D/eps0':>8} {'Delta(meV)':>11} {'+/-':>7}   R(1.2K)  R(40K)")
for j in range(0, len(Dgrid), max(1, len(Dgrid) // 14)):
    print(f"{Dgrid[j]:+8.3f} {gaps[j]:11.3f} {gerr[j]:7.3f}   {Rmat[0, j]:8.1f} {Rmat[-1, j]:8.1f}")

k0 = int(np.argmin(np.abs(Dgrid)))
print(f"\nDelta at D = {Dgrid[k0]:+.3f} V/nm : {gaps[k0]:+.3f} +/- {gerr[k0]:.3f} meV"
      f"   (NEGATIVE = metallic, dR/dT > 0)")

# INVERSION-SYMMETRY TEST: where does Delta(D) MINIMISE? Not the intercept of a linear fit
# to the +D flank — Delta(D) is plainly curved near its minimum, so extrapolating a straight
# line back to zero is meaningless. ABCA must minimise at D = 0; ABCB at finite D.
near = np.abs(Dgrid - Dgrid[int(np.argmin(gaps))]) < 0.12
q = np.polyfit(Dgrid[near], gaps[near], 2)
D_gapmin = -q[1] / (2 * q[0])
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
boot = []
for _ in range(400):
    yy = gaps[near] + rng.normal(0, np.maximum(gerr[near], 1e-3))
    qq = np.polyfit(Dgrid[near], yy, 2)
    if qq[0] > 0:
        boot.append(-qq[1] / (2 * qq[0]))
bs = float(np.std(boot)) if len(boot) > 50 else float("nan")
print(f"\nDelta(D) minimum (parabola over {int(near.sum())} pts): "
      f"D = {D_gapmin:+.3f} +/- {bs:.3f} V/nm")
print(f"  run 3's R_CNP minimum sat at D = 0.000 +/- 0.008 V/nm — consistent")
print(f"  ABCA requires this at D = 0; ABCB requires it clearly displaced")

hi = Dgrid > 0.13
jm = int(np.argmax(gaps))
print(f"\nDelta rises at {np.polyfit(Dgrid[hi], gaps[hi], 1)[0]:.1f} meV per V/nm on the "
      f"+D flank, peaking at {gaps[jm]:.2f} +/- {gerr[jm]:.2f} meV at D = {Dgrid[jm]:+.3f}")
cross = Dgrid[np.argmin(np.abs(gaps))]
print(f"dR/dT changes sign at D = {cross:+.3f} V/nm: METALLIC below, INSULATING above — "
      f"a displacement-field-driven metal-insulator crossover at charge neutrality.")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(17, 4.8))
for (Tm, D, Rc, rid) in curves:
    ax[0].plot(D, Rc, lw=1.1, label=f"{Tm:.1f} K")
ax[0].set_yscale("log"); ax[0].set_xlabel("D/eps0 (V/nm)"); ax[0].set_ylabel("R_CNP (ohm)")
ax[0].axvline(cross, ls=":", c="k", lw=1.0)
ax[0].set_title("R at neutrality vs D, per temperature"); ax[0].legend(fontsize=7)

for dt in (0.0, 0.10, 0.20, 0.28):
    j = int(np.argmin(np.abs(Dgrid - dt)))
    ax[1].plot(1 / Ts, Rmat[:, j], "o-", ms=5, label=f"D={Dgrid[j]:+.2f}")
ax[1].set_yscale("log"); ax[1].set_xlabel("1/T (1/K)"); ax[1].set_ylabel("R_CNP (ohm)")
ax[1].set_title("Arrhenius"); ax[1].legend(fontsize=7); ax[1].grid(alpha=0.3)

ax[2].errorbar(Dgrid, gaps, yerr=gerr, fmt="o-", ms=4, lw=1.0, capsize=2)
ax[2].axhline(0, ls="--", c="k", lw=0.9); ax[2].axvline(0, ls="--", c="k", lw=0.9)
ax[2].axvline(D_gapmin, ls=":", c="r", lw=1.2)
ax[2].set_xlabel("D/eps0 (V/nm)"); ax[2].set_ylabel("activation gap Delta (meV)")
ax[2].set_title(f"Delta(D), minimum at {D_gapmin:+.3f} V/nm")
ax[2].grid(alpha=0.3)
fig.tight_layout()

ana 33

Read: a displacement-field-driven metal–insulator crossover at charge neutrality, and a gap that is real but small.

At D ≈ 0 the neutrality point is metallic — Δ = −0.62 ± 0.17 meV, i.e. R_CNP rises with temperature (249 Ω at 1.2 K → 360 Ω at 40 K). By D/ε₀ = +0.238 V/nm it is insulating — Δ = +1.36 ± 0.14 meV, R_CNP falling 2975 Ω → 1175 Ω over the same range. The sign of dR/dT flips at D = +0.126 V/nm, and all seven isotherms cross at that single point. The +D flank rises at 7.9 meV per V/nm.

This is the cleanest exclusion of ABAB in the session. A Bernal tetralayer is a band-overlapped semimetal: displacement field gaps each bilayer-like subband but shifts them relative to one another, so the overlap survives and neutrality stays metallic at all D. A metal→insulator crossover driven purely by D is not that.

The inversion-symmetry test, done properly. Δ(D) is plainly curved near its minimum, so extrapolating a straight line from the +D flank back to zero — which an earlier version of this cell did, returning a meaningless −1.12 meV intercept — is the wrong statistic. The right one is where the minimum sits. A parabola over the 29 points around it gives D = +0.016 ± 0.004 V/nm, against run 3's independent R_CNP minimum at 0.000 ± 0.008 V/nm. Both sit within ~4 % of the accessible D range of zero.

But the magnitude does not behave like a clean band gap, and that is the honest limit here. 1.36 meV at D ≈ 0.25 V/nm is one to two orders of magnitude below what a rhombohedral tetralayer's single-particle gap should be at that field. Together with R_CNP's saturation near 3 kΩ (run 3), this says the transport is disorder- and parallel-channel-limited: in-gap states and a shunt path put a floor under the resistance long before the true gap would. That is entirely ordinary for gapped graphene multilayers — measured activation energies routinely run 10–30× below the band gap — but it means this measurement establishes the gap's existence and D-dependence, not its size. Any claim of the form "the gap is X meV" is not supported; "a gap opens with |D| and closes near D = 0" is.

The base-temperature point is excluded from every fit: R_CNP is flat between 1.2 and 8 K, exactly as the rig's ~8 K electron temperature predicts, so those points carry no independent information.

analysis of this data — The call — <device> stacking order (ana 34–34)
ana 34

The call — <device> stacking order

1. Per-region verdict

region (contact pair)verdictstrength
B_1 – B_2 (the only four-terminal region wired this cooldown)ABCA — rhombohedralmoderate

"Region-resolved" is one region. The device card's provided configuration wires exactly one four-terminal pair; T_1–T_4 are dead. Stacking domains elsewhere in the flake are untested, and per the brief that is an operator rewiring matter, not a detour I could take.

2. Evidence

(a) A displacement field opens a gap at charge neutrality — data/3. R_CNP rises 10.4×, from 296 Ω at D ≈ 0 to 3074 Ω at D/ε₀ = +0.307 V/nm, measured over ~30 crossings of the neutrality line. The session's own gate calibration comes from the same run: the CNP-line slope over 26 unambiguous rows gives c_tg/c_bg = 1.2737 ± 0.0470 (the geometry prior was 1.1579), and every later cell used the measured ratio.

(b) The gap is centred on D = 0 — data/3 and data/6–data/12. Two independent observables locate the minimum:

  • R_CNP at base temperature: D = 0.000 ± 0.008 V/nm, with the folded branches agreeing to within 7 % — R(+D)/R(−D) = 1.07, 1.01, 1.03, 0.96 at |ΔD| = 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08 V/nm, against a ~3 % per-point noise floor. Robust to ±1σ on the capacitance ratio (moves it < 0.001 V/nm).
  • The activation gap Δ(D): minimum at D = +0.016 ± 0.004 V/nm.

(c) Neutrality crosses from metallic to insulating under D — data/6–data/12. Δ = −0.62 ± 0.17 meV at D ≈ 0 (R_CNP rises with T: 249 → 360 Ω from 1.2 to 40 K) and +1.36 ± 0.14 meV at D = +0.238 V/nm (R_CNP falls 2975 → 1175 Ω). dR/dT changes sign at D = +0.126 V/nm; all seven isotherms cross there. +D flank slope 7.9 meV per V/nm.

(d) A single Fermi pocket — data/5, corroborated by data/4. Four of five densities return exactly one unflagged SdH tone and none returns two; the two highest-contrast traces (n = +0.99 and +1.49 × 10¹² cm⁻²) give f/f_full = 0.835 and 0.834. Two pockets would put the dominant tone near 0.7× the full Onsager value and add a second near 0.3×, both scaling linearly with n. Neither is present. Cross-check: the density scale implied by the SdH slope (α = 1.199) agrees with the Landau fan's independent minima-ladder (α = 1.166) to 2.8 %.

Why not ABAB. Two independent disqualifications. A Bernal tetralayer is a band-overlapped semimetal whose neutrality point stays conducting under displacement field — but (c) shows a clean D-driven metal→insulator crossover. And its two bilayer-like bands both cross E_F at D = 0, which must produce two SdH tones at a fixed ratio — but (d) finds one.

Why not ABCB. ABCB lacks inversion symmetry, so it carries a built-in gap at D = 0 that is closed by a field of one particular sign; its gap minimum must sit at finite D. Both independent estimates put the minimum within ~4 % of the accessible D range of zero.

3. Confidence and hedges

Moderate, not strong. Five things hold it back, in order of how much they matter:

  1. The −D lever arm is only 0.26 of +D. Negative D at neutrality requires V_tg < 0, and the provided top-gate limit stops at −0.3 V — an operating limit the brief bans me from probing. Symmetry is therefore demonstrated over |D| ≤ 0.10 V/nm, not the full range. An ABCB asymmetry that only develops beyond that would be invisible here. This is the single biggest limitation on the call.
  2. The two estimates of the gap-minimum location do not perfectly agree: 0.000 ± 0.008 (base-T resistance) versus +0.016 ± 0.004 V/nm (activation). Taken at face value the second is displaced from zero by several times its own fit error. I do not read that as evidence for ABCB — the two are different observables, the bootstrap error captures only fit noise, and 0.016 V/nm is 4 % of the accessible range — but a weak inversion-symmetry breaking cannot be excluded by this dataset.
  3. The gap's magnitude is not a band-structure number. Δ_max = 1.36 meV is one to two orders of magnitude below a clean rhombohedral gap at D ≈ 0.25 V/nm, and R_CNP saturates near 3 kΩ rather than continuing up. Transport is disorder- and parallel-channel-limited. The gap's existence and D-dependence are established; its size is not.
  4. No absolute density calibration. The SdH frequency and the LL ladder both depend only on the product α·g (measured consistently as 4.78 and 4.67), so the density scale and the Landau degeneracy cannot be separated. Breaking the degeneracy needs R_xy = B/(n·e), and no Hall pair is wired — sr2 and sr3 are n.c. Assuming the standard g = 4 gives c_tg = 2.40 mF/m² (11.1 nm equivalent hBN against the card's 9.5 nm). Nothing above depends on this: the evidence is a ratio, a symmetry point, and a tone count.
  5. No Hall-bar geometry, so every resistance here is in ohms, not ohms per square, and no absolute sheet-resistance or mobility claim is made. Electron temperature ~8 K also puts correlated and symmetry-broken states out of reach and restricts the activation fit to T ≥ 8 K.

What was not measured, and why. The Si contact-doping gate stayed at 0 V all session (the graphite back gate screens it from the channel, so it was never needed; its ramp is consent-gated). No field above 6 T, because the magnet's fixed 0.137 T/min made every extra tesla ~7 min each way and 6 T already put ν = ±8 inside the density window. No measurement below 8 K carries independent information.

What would overturn the call.

  • Extending the top-gate range past −0.3 V to lengthen the −D lever arm, and finding the gap minimum genuinely displaced → ABCB. This is the decisive follow-up.
  • A second SdH tone below ~1.5 T, which the degree-5 background removal would have eaten → would reopen a two-pocket (ABAB-like) reading. A lower-field, finer 1/B record would test it.
  • A Hall pair, giving an absolute density and hence the true Landau degeneracy — this would not touch the D-symmetry or tone-count arguments, but it would let the LL sequence be read independently instead of assumed.

4. One correction to the record

The proposing cell for the Landau fan (measure notebook, idx 41) claimed the LL degeneracy would discriminate ABCA from ABAB — that a rhombohedral tetralayer's 4-fold orbital zero level (16 states, first gaps at ν = ±8) would look different from a Bernal one. That is wrong. ABAB tetralayer decomposes into two effective bilayers, each with a 2-fold orbital zero level × 4 spin/valley = 8 states, and both sit at exactly E = 0 — so ABAB also has 16 zero-energy states. The zero-LL degeneracy is 4N for N layers regardless of stacking order: it counts layers, not stacking. The measure notebook is append-only so the claim stands there; this is the correction. The fan's actual contribution to the call is the pocket count, not the degeneracy.

HERA — close-out: return-to-initial

16:10 · close-out return-to-initial: heaters off, TG/BG to 0 V at 5 mV/step, field to 0 T, full readback of field/gates/leakage/temperatures · ETA ~16:20 (≈10 min)

The brief's close-out step. Order matters: heaters off first, so the sample begins cooling from 40 K while the gates and field ramp; then both Keithley gates to 0 V at their committed 5 mV/step pacing; then the field to zero (it is already at +0.006 T, where the ladder left it, so this is a no-op guarded by a read). Finally a full readback of field, gates, leakage, temperatures and heater ranges for the session log.

Si is not touched. It sat at 0.000 V all session — the graphite back gate screens it from the channel, so it was never needed — and the DC205 ramp is consent-gated. The cell reads it and flags it for the operator rather than ramping it.

Lock-in settings are deliberately NOT restored to state0. sr1 sensitivity (2 µV → 1 mV) and sr0/sr1 τ (0.3 → 0.1 s) were changed with operator authorisation because the session-start values were wrong for this device — sr1 was railed at 2 µV before the first sweep. Restoring them would hand the next session a known-bad configuration. The readback records what they actually are.

ERRATUM — correcting cell idx 41 (the P4 Landau-fan proposal) measure 50–50

measure 50

ERRATUM — correcting cell idx 41 (the P4 Landau-fan proposal)

This notebook is append-only, so the erroneous claim below stays on the page. This cell is the marker a reader needs.

Cell idx 41 (## HERA — P4: Landau fan at D = 0) states: "a rhombohedral N-layer stack carries an N-fold orbitally degenerate zero-energy level; for tetralayer ABCA that is 4 × 4 (spin×valley) = 16 states, so the first flanking gaps fall at ν = ±8. A Bernal tetralayer decomposes into two bilayer-like sets whose levels arrive at different fields, giving a visibly different sequence. Counting filling factors settles it on band structure alone."

That is wrong. ABAB tetralayer decomposes into two effective bilayers, each carrying a 2-fold orbital zero level × 4 spin/valley = 8 states, and both sit at exactly E = 0 — so ABAB also has 16 zero-energy states, identical to ABCA. The zero-Landau-level degeneracy is 4N for N layers regardless of stacking order: it counts layers, not stacking. Counting filling factors therefore does not settle ABCA vs ABAB.

What run 4 actually contributes to the stacking call is the Fermi-pocket count — one SdH tone proportional to n, where two bilayer-like bands would give two — plus a cross-check on the density scale. Neither depends on the retracted claim, and the run was worth doing. See the ana notebook (Run 4 — landau-fan) and the final call for the corrected reasoning.

No measurement, setpoint or datum is affected by this erratum; it corrects reasoning only.

HERA — mandated close-out: close_out(restore=state0) measure 51–52

measure 51

HERA — mandated close-out: close_out(restore=state0)

16:42 · mandated close_out((magnet.field, 0.0), restore=state0) with explicit heater/gate stages and extra readback; restores sr1 sens to 2 uV and sr0/sr1 tau to 0.3 s · ETA ~16:47 (≈5 min)

Run at the operator's explicit instruction, superseding the hand-written close-out at idx 49. close_out() is the canonical helper: it replays state0 param-by-param in capture order, steps the named excitation/heater/gate stages, lands the field at an explicit endpoint (never defaulted), and prints a full readback with validator suffixes.

Field endpoint: 0.0 T, stated explicitly rather than "hold". The magnet is already at +0.006 T from the previous close-out, so this is a no-op guarded by a real set.

What restore=state0 puts back, and one consequence worth naming. state0 (idx 27) was captured at bring-up, before the acquisition was re-ranged. Replaying it returns sr1 sensitivity to 2 µV and sr0/sr1 τ to 0.3 s — the configuration in which sr1 was railed (fs = 1.01 at the zero-gate operating point) and which made the compliant dwell 2.1 s/pt. That is genuinely what "restore the initial state" means, and it is not a safety matter: an SR830 input overload is a normal operating condition, and the gates and field are already at zero. But the next session should know that 2 µV is a known-bad starting sensitivity for this device at 10 nA bias, not a considered default — see session_notes.md.

Si: state0 restores V_si through dc205.smart_voltage(0.0), which is a DC205 ramp call. Si has sat at 0.000 V all session, so this is a zero-length ramp; the DC205 ramp is consent-gated and the operator's instruction to run close_out(restore=state0) is that consent.

Heaters and both Keithley gates are listed as explicit stages as well as being in state0 — close_out dedupes by parameter identity, so each appears once in the readback.

(n, D) — capacitance-based convention

GateCalibration carries the gate->(n, D) lever arm: cal.n_D(V_tg, V_bg) returns n in SI (m^-2; ×1e-16 for 10^12 cm^-2) and D in V/m. Build it from the gate-stack thicknesses with from_thicknesses (κ_hBN/κ_SiO2 default). This is the capacitance convention, not the toploader's dtg/dbg constant form. Set n_offset / D_offset from the session's gate calibration once the CNP / D-line is live.
